gen.title: How a Preliminary Declaration Became a Limited Military Measure
gen.orderNote: Follow the cause to effect order as the text introduces each change

steps.label: Preliminary Emancipation Proclamation
steps.quote: That changed on September 22, 1862, when President Lincoln issued his Preliminary Emancipation Proclamation

steps.label: would be declared free
steps.quote: which stated that enslaved people in those states or parts of states still in rebellion as of January 1, 1863, would be declared free.

steps.label: Emancipation Proclamation
steps.quote: One hundred days later, with the rebellion unabated, President issued the Emancipation Proclamation declaring

steps.label: military measure
steps.quote: Lincoln’s bold step to change the goals of the war was a military measure and came just a few days after the Union’s victory in the Battle of Antietam
steps.orderHint: Measure is defined as military action

steps.label: loyal border states
steps.quote: It applied only to states that had seceded from the Union, leaving slavery untouched in the loyal border states.
steps.orderHint: Scope is limited to seceded states

steps.label: exempted parts of the Confederacy
steps.quote: It also expressly exempted parts of the Confederacy that had already come under Union control.

steps.label: freedom it promised
steps.quote: Most important, the freedom it promised depended upon Union military victory.
